Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale: Items and real responses

Source: R/data.R
rses.Rd

The ten items of the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES; Rosenberg, 1965) and the answers of 47,974 people who took it online through the Open-Source Psychometrics Project. The RSES is short and widely used, and its items have well-documented problems, so it is a test case for the pretest, the cognitive interviews and the benchmark (see sc_builtin_instrument()).

Usage

rses_items

rses_real

Format

rses_items: A data frame with 10 rows and 6 columns: item (RSE1 to RSE10), scale (SE), scale_label (Self-esteem), statement, reverse (TRUE for the five negatively worded items) and issue (the reported problem, or NA).

rses_real: A data frame with 47,974 rows and 13 columns: country (two-letter code from the respondent's network address, or NA; the largest groups are US (22,451), GB (6,672) and CA (2,941)), gender (factor: Male, Female or Other), age (13 to 99, other entries NA) and the ten items.

An object of class data.frame with 10 rows and 6 columns.

An object of class data.frame with 47974 rows and 13 columns.

Source

Open-Source Psychometrics Project, https://openpsychometrics.org/_rawdata/ (RSE data; only respondents who confirmed that their answers were accurate and could be used for research). The project gives no formal licence for the data. The items are free to use; the script is data-raw/instruments.R in the package's GitHub repository.

Details

Known problems. The five negatively worded items (3, 5, 8, 9 and 10) share variance beyond self-esteem: A one-factor model fits poorly, and a second factor or a method factor for negative wording is needed (Marsh, 1996; Tomás & Oliver, 1999; DiStefano & Motl, 2006). How the negative items behave also differs across cultures (Schmitt & Allik, 2005). Item 8 ("I wish I could have more respect for myself") is often the weakest item. In rses_real it has the lowest corrected item-total correlation (0.54; the others are 0.59 to 0.75). The issue column of rses_items gives a one-line note per item.

Answers are on a 4-point scale (1 = strongly disagree, 2 = disagree, 3 = agree, 4 = strongly agree) and are stored as given: Reverse-keyed items are not reversed. Use rses_items$reverse and 5 - x before scoring. Unanswered items (coded 0 in the original file) are NA.

References

DiStefano, C., & Motl, R. W. (2006). Further investigating method effects associated with negatively worded items on self-report surveys. Structural Equation Modeling, 13(3), 440-464. doi:10.1207/s15328007sem1303_6

Marsh, H. W. (1996). Positive and negative global self-esteem: A substantively meaningful distinction or artifactors? Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 70(4), 810-819. doi:10.1037/0022-3514.70.4.810

Rosenberg, M. (1965). Society and the adolescent self-image. Princeton University Press.

Schmitt, D. P., & Allik, J. (2005). Simultaneous administration of the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale in 53 nations. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 89(4), 623-642. doi:10.1037/0022-3514.89.4.623

Tomás, J. M., & Oliver, A. (1999). Rosenberg's self-esteem scale: Two factors or method effects. Structural Equation Modeling, 6(1), 84-98. doi:10.1080/10705519909540120

See also

sc_builtin_instrument(), dass_items, mini_ipip_items

Examples

rses_items[, c("item", "reverse", "statement")]
#>     item reverse
#> 1   RSE1   FALSE
#> 2   RSE2   FALSE
#> 3   RSE3    TRUE
#> 4   RSE4   FALSE
#> 5   RSE5    TRUE
#> 6   RSE6   FALSE
#> 7   RSE7   FALSE
#> 8   RSE8    TRUE
#> 9   RSE9    TRUE
#> 10 RSE10    TRUE
#>                                                                      statement
#> 1  I feel that I am a person of worth, at least on an equal plane with others.
#> 2                               I feel that I have a number of good qualities.
#> 3                       All in all, I am inclined to feel that I am a failure.
#> 4                         I am able to do things as well as most other people.
#> 5                                    I feel I do not have much to be proud of.
#> 6                                    I take a positive attitude toward myself.
#> 7                                    On the whole, I am satisfied with myself.
#> 8                                 I wish I could have more respect for myself.
#> 9                                           I certainly feel useless at times.
#> 10                                       At times I think I am no good at all.
x <- rses_real[rses_items$item]
x[rses_items$reverse] <- 5 - x[rses_items$reverse]
summary(rowMeans(x, na.rm = TRUE))
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.     NAs 
#>   1.000   2.100   2.600   2.630   3.111   4.000      45
